newsitem.title: UK: UK's BG sees higher profit, waits for MMC report.
newsitem.headline: UK's BG sees higher profit, waits for MMC report.

text.p: British gas pipeline operator BG Plc on Thursday reported higher first-quarter profits, but added its outlook remains uncertain ahead of a crucial report on proposed price changes.
Pre-tax profit rose to 615 million pounds ($1 billion) from 560 million ahead of the report from the Monopolies and Mergers Commision (MMC), which is expected to come out in June.
"The group's short-term prospects do remain dominated by the MMC inquiry," finance director Philip Hampton told Reuters in an interview.
The MMC started its inquiry in October after BG rejected new price proposals from watchdog Ofgas.
BG said the proposals, which would regulate charges to gas suppliers for pumping gas through BG's pipelines, as too strict.
The company warned that implementation would cost it 400 million pounds in annual cash flow, while investors fear a hefty dividend cut.
The first-quarter profit rise would not give fresh ammunition to Ofgas to defend its tough stance Hampton said.
"The results are only satisfactory. We still think that we are not making a generous return on our asset base," he said.
"This quarter is typically our best when the weather is coldest in our major market," Hampton added.
Besides the MMC inquiry, BG also faces the uncertainty of Labour's planned tax on privatised utilities' windfall profits.
Hampton said BG had no reliable information on the size of the levy or how it might affect BG in particular.
No provision for the the planned windfall tax was therefore made.
BG is the renamed rump of British Gas following the demerger of the gas supply business in February. ($ = 0.608 British Pounds)
